2607.07003.title: Dissociating the Internal Representations of Sycophancy in LLMs
2607.07003.paper_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) frequently exhibit sycophancy, where they agree with a user's statement even when incorrect. While sycophancy is often treated as a single defined behavior, it can manifest in substantially distinct ways and circumstances, raising the question of whether this multi-faceted nature is reflected in its internal mechanisms. To address this gap, we dissociate the representations of sycophancy into factual and opinion subtypes -- motivated by the distinction between verifiable claims and subjective beliefs. We train linear probes and construct steering vectors on activations of one subtype and evaluate their transfer to the other subtype to measure to what extent they share representations. We find evidence that different LLMs represent these subtypes differently, with either more unified or more distinct and causally interfering representations. This method of dissociation offers a promising framework for studying the representational structure of complex model behaviors.
2607.07003.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）經常表現出阿諛奉承的行為，即使在不正確的情況下也會同意用戶的陳述。雖然阿諛奉承通常被視為一種單一的定義行為，但它可以在實質上以不同的方式和情境表現出來，這引發了這種多面性是否反映在其內部機制中的問題。為了解決這一差距，我們將阿諛奉承的表徵分離為事實和意見兩種類型——這是基於可驗證主張和主觀信念之間的區別。我們訓練線性探針並在一種類型的激活上構建引導向量，並評估它們向另一種類型的轉移，以測量它們在多大程度上共享表徵。我們發現不同的LLMs以不同的方式表示這些類型，有的表徵更統一，有的則更獨特且因果干擾。這種分離的方法為研究複雜模型行為的表徵結構提供了一個有前景的框架。
